01 / The challenge

The challenge for mobile mechanics.

A mobile mechanic often works at the kerbside or on a customer’s driveway. The van needs to say exactly what you do and show a number that someone with a broken-down car can read quickly.

01

Roadside visibility

Your van might be parked in a lay-by or on a driveway. The service has to be clear.

02

Lots of services

Servicing, diagnostics, tyres and batteries — which do you lead with?

03

Oil and grime

Graphics need to clean up easily.

02 / What to include

What your van must say.

  • Business name
  • Mobile mechanic, tyres or diagnostics
  • Phone number, large
  • Area covered

Not sure what to include? Our guide to what to put on a work van walks you through it.

06 / Design tips

Build the layout around the job.

01

Lead with the service

Mobile mechanic or mobile tyre fitting should be the first thing people read after your name.

02

Keep the number big

Someone broken down needs to read it quickly.

03

Use durable film

Choose a laminated film that can be cleaned without damage.

Before you book

Good to know.

Can the graphics be cleaned with degreaser?

Use a mild cleaner where possible. We will give you aftercare advice for the film we fit.

Can you add a list of services?

Yes. Keep it to three or four short items so it stays readable.

Do you brand recovery trucks?

Yes. Send the body type and photos and mention any required markings.
